summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of steal syndrome was admitted due to altered mental status and weakness after receiving an incomplete dialysis session and excess oxycodone. He was found to have a supratherapeutic digoxin level, likely due to daily administration at his rehab facility instead of every other day. His confusion improved after holding digoxin and narcotics, and completing hemodialysis. Hyperkalemia and mild pulmonary edema resolved with dialysis. Hypercalcemia was detected, and PTH was elevated, leading to the diagnosis of hyperparathyroidism and initiation of cinacalcet. Atrial flutter was observed but remained asymptomatic. Pain management was optimized with acetaminophen, lidocaine patches, and low-dose oxycodone to avoid sedation. He was discharged to extended care with stable mental status, clear instructions on digoxin dosing, and follow-up plans for pain, neurology, and palliative care.
problems: Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, unspecified
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
